competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and unchanged per Q3 2026 10-Q Part II Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Millrose's primary business remains concentrated with Lennar, which has no obligation to offer new business and may use competing land-banking providers or deem Millrose's terms uncompetitive.
quotes: Since the Spin-Off, our primary business and source of revenues have been and will continue to be from Lennar pursuant to the Lennar Agreements.

As a result, Lennar may choose not to offer us additional business for any reason, including utilizing traditional land banking arrangements, engaging other providers, or determining that the terms of the Lennar Agreements are not competitive.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and unchanged per Q3 2026 10-Q Part II Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Lennar's exclusive Founder's Rights—including a Capital Priority Right and Enforcement Rights—restrict capital available for non-Lennar deals, reduce negotiating leverage with other builders, and may deter third-party counterparties.
quotes: Additionally, Lennar’s Capital Priority Right limits the amount of capital Millrose has available for transactions with counterparties other than Lennar or Lennar Related Ventures, which may make it difficult to provide our homesite option platform to such counterparties.

Certain Lennar Agreements, including the Founder’s Right Agreement, include rights exclusive to Lennar that we cannot offer to Other Counterparties, which may reduce our negotiating leverage with Other Counterparties.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and unchanged per Q3 2026 10-Q Part II Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: The Lennar Agreements prohibit third-party financing that causes the combined debt-to-equity ratio to exceed 1:1 without Lennar's prior approval, limiting Millrose's ability to fund counterparties via debt structures.
quotes: Under the Lennar Agreements, Millrose may not enter into third-party financing arrangements that would cause the combined debt-to-equity ratio of Millrose and its affiliates to exceed 1:1 without Lennar’s prior approval.
This restriction may limit our ability to provide funding to counterparties who prefer to structure their relationships with us through debt issuances.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and unchanged per Q3 2026 10-Q Part II Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Because counterparties are not obligated to exercise purchase options, a severe market downturn or counterparty bankruptcy could halt option exercises, leave Millrose reselling properties below cost, or render key agreements unenforceable.
quotes: However, our counterparties are under no obligation to exercise their land purchase options and purchase the homesites, and they may decline to exercise them in the event of a significant downturn in the market.
If we or any of our major counterparties, including Lennar, enter into bankruptcy, key agreements such as the Master Program Agreement or the Master Option Agreement may become unenforceable.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Item 7 MD&A.

This geographic concentration may increase our exposure to market fluctuations and environmental risks, as discussed elsewhere in this “Risk Factors” section.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and unchanged per Q3 2026 10-Q Part II Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Millrose has not obtained independent appraisals or Phase I environmental reports for Spin-Off and Rausch assets and could bear direct remediation costs for construction-related environmental liabilities outside predetermined development budgets.
quotes: We have not obtained independent appraisals or valuations for our real estate assets, including the assets acquired in the Spin-Off and the Rausch Transaction.

We have not obtained Phase I or similar environmental reports from independent consultants for our real estate assets, including those acquired in the Spin-Off from Lennar and in the Rausch Transaction.

Predetermined development budgets do not cover liabilities arising from construction, and construction activity could result in environmental consequences that we may be required to remediate, which could significantly reduce our available cash and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

The 2029 Notes mature on October 15, 2029 and the 2031 Notes mature on October 15, 2031.

This could significantly reduce our cash flow and jeopardize our ability to maintain working capital and make required distributions to qualify as a REIT.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the financial statements and management discussion in F2, P4, and P6.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the risk factors in P2.
growth_thesis.claim: Sustaining the recycled capital business model requires counterparties to continue electing to exercise their land purchase options, as they are under no contractual obligation to purchase homesites.
quotes: The continued sustainability of Millrose’s recycled capital business model, which is intended to generally provide Millrose with reliable, consistent and uninterrupted access to capital, is contingent on our counterparties electing to exercise their land purchase options.

However, our counterparties are under no obligation to exercise their land purchase options and purchase the homesites, and they may decline to exercise them in the event of a significant downturn in the market.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the annual and quarterly portfolio disclosures and earnings release in P3, P4, and P6.
growth_thesis.claim: Millrose expanded its counterparty base from 15 at December 31, 2025 to 22 homebuilder and developer relationships as of September 30, 2026, growing Invested Capital under Other Agreements to $3,371,171 (table in thousands) at a 10.8% weighted average yield versus 8.5% under the Master Program Agreement.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, we had 142,139 homesites with 15 counterparties which were included in 66 separate pools, in accordance with the applicable Multiparty Cross Agreements.
We funded $714.4 million for land acquisition and development and received $192.8 million in net takedown proceeds for Other Agreements during this period at a weighted average yield of 10.8%.

This capital growth of approximately $521 million compared to the prior quarter reflects the organic expansion of Millrose's business model, including the continued diversification of its builder base to 21 counterparties outside of Lennar.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the risk factors in P2.
growth_thesis.claim: Continued non-Lennar expansion requires successfully negotiating agreements with additional homebuilders while managing Lennar’s Capital Priority Right and exclusive Founder’s Rights.
quotes: While Millrose has acquired other homebuilders as new counterparties, there is no guarantee that Millrose will continue to be successful in negotiating agreements with additional counterparties.

Additionally, Lennar’s Capital Priority Right limits the amount of capital Millrose has available for transactions with counterparties other than Lennar or Lennar Related Ventures, which may make it difficult to provide our homesite option platform to such counterparties.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1, P4, and P6, and reflected in preferred instruments on the balance sheet and income statement in F1 and F2.
growth_thesis.claim: Millrose has driven asset growth by providing large-scale M&A capital support, including $494.5 million for New Home’s acquisition of Landsea and approximately $1.068 billion in combined preferred instrument and homesite funding for Dream Finders’ acquisition of Beazer Homes.
quotes: On June 25, 2025, New Home completed the acquisition of Landsea and we funded land banking capital of $494.5 million at closing, acquiring a portfolio of homesites, subject to option agreements with New Home.
Total funding provided by the Company to Dream Finders was approximately $1.068 billion.

With the completion of the Dream Finders financing, approximately 42% of our asset base is now invested outside the Lennar Master Program Agreement, reflecting what Millrose has always been: a comprehensive capital solutions platform for the homebuilding industry.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P2 regarding the leverage cap and financing uncertainty, and inferred from rising debt and interest expense in F1, F2, P4, and P8.
growth_thesis.claim: Funding large M&A and portfolio expansions requires continued access to debt financing on favorable terms without violating the 1:1 combined debt-to-equity ratio limit under the Lennar Agreements.
quotes: Under the Lennar Agreements, Millrose may not enter into third-party financing arrangements that would cause the combined debt-to-equity ratio of Millrose and its affiliates to exceed 1:1 without Lennar’s prior approval.
However, there can be no assurance that such financing will be obtained or will be sufficient to cover all of our planned initiatives.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 and P6 and reflected on the balance sheet in F1.

quotes: The land banking facility represents the Company’s first multifamily land banking partnership, under which it will acquire and fund development of homesites and execute option agreements with JPI during the development period.

During the third quarter of 2026, the Company acquired 1,233 single-family residential properties from Lennar for approximately $333 million, inclusive of acquisition costs and capitalized property costs, which was financed with borrowings of approximately $213 million under our SFR Secured Credit Facility and cash on hand.

The Company has entered into agreements with Lennar to acquire 620 additional single-family residential properties for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $150.3 million, with an expected net investment of approximately $50 million after anticipated asset-level limited recourse financing.

material_events.claim: Millrose completed its Spin-Off from Lennar through a distribution of approximately 80% of its Common Stock, listed its Class A common stock on the NYSE under the symbol MRP, received approximately $5.5 billion in land assets and approximately $1.0 billion in cash, and entered into a Revolving Credit Agreement up to $1.335 billion.

In addition, Millrose entered into the Revolving Credit Agreement with a commitment amount of up to $1.335 billion (together with the Revolving Credit Agreement, the “Revolving Credit Facility”) that is scheduled to mature on February 7, 2028.
